items.title: The Six Elements' Substance and Their Particular and Universal Characteristics

items.zh: 又正尋思地等六界內外差別，發起勝解。如是名為尋思界事。又正尋思：地為堅相，乃至風為輕動相，識為了別相，空界為虛空相、遍滿色相、無障礙相。是名尋思諸界自相。又正尋思：此一切界，以要言之，皆是無常乃至無我。是名尋思諸界共相。
items.en: One further rightly investigates the inner and outer distinction among earth and the other six elements, giving rise to a vivid understanding — this is called investigating the substance of the elements. One further rightly investigates: earth has the mark of solidity … wind has the mark of light movement, consciousness has the mark of discernment, and the space element has the mark of empty space, pervading form, and being unobstructed. This is called investigating the particular characteristics of the elements. One further rightly investigates: all these elements, in brief, are impermanent, and so on through being without self. This is called investigating the universal characteristic of the elements.

items.title: Section: Category, Time, and Principle — Elemental Analysis Closes

items.zh: 又正尋思於一合相界差別性。不了知者，由界差別所合成身，發起高慢，便為顛倒，黑品所攝，廣說如前。與上相違，便無顛倒，白品所攝，廣說如前。如是名為尋思界品。
items.en: One further rightly investigates: if one fails to understand the differentiated nature of the elements within what appears as a single unified mass, and, on account of the body formed by this combination of elements, gives rise to arrogance, this is a distortion, belonging to the dark category, as extensively explained before. The reverse of this is free of distortion, belonging to the bright category, as extensively explained before. This is called investigating the category of the elements.

items.zh: 又正尋思：去來今世六界為緣，得入母胎。如是名為尋思界時。又正尋思：如草木等眾緣和合，圍遶虛空，數名為舍。如是六界為所依故，筋骨血肉眾緣和合，圍遶虛空，假想、等想施設言論，數名為身。復由宿世諸業煩惱及自種子以為因緣。如是名依觀待道理尋思諸界差別道理。
items.en: One further rightly investigates: in past, present, and future lives alike, the six elements serve as conditions for entry into the womb. This is called investigating the time of the elements. One further rightly investigates: just as grass, wood, and other conditions combine to enclose empty space and are provisionally called "a dwelling," so too, depending on these six elements, sinew, bone, blood, and flesh combine to enclose empty space, and through provisional, conventional conception one sets up the expression and provisionally calls it "a body." Further, this depends on karma and affliction accumulated across past lives, together with one's own seeds, as causes and conditions. This is called investigating the principles of the elements by way of the principle of mutual dependence.

items.zh: 又正尋思：若於如是界差別觀善修、善習、善多修習，能斷憍慢。又正尋思：如是道理，有至教量，有內證智，有比度法，有成立法性、難思法性、安住法性。如是名依作用道理、證成道理、法爾道理尋思諸界差別道理。是名勤修界差別觀者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那。

items.title: Section: Breath-Counting Contemplation Opens — the Fifth and Final Purifying-Conduct Object

items.zh: 云何勤修阿那波那念者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那？謂依入出息念增上正法聽聞受持增上力故，能正了知於入出息所緣境界，繫心了達，無忘明記，是阿那波那念義。如是名為尋思其義。
items.en: How does one who diligently cultivates mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath investigate insight with objects differentiated by the six things? That is, by the empowering force of having heard and upheld the excellent teaching on mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath, one is able to correctly know the object that is the in-breath and out-breath, binding the mind to it and comprehending it, without forgetting, held clearly in mind. This is the meaning of mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath.

items.zh: 又正尋思：入息、出息在內可得；繫屬身故，外處攝故，內外差別。如是名為尋思其事。又正尋思：入息有二，出息有二。若風入內，名為入息；若風出外、名為出息。
items.en: One further rightly investigates: the in-breath and out-breath can be found within the body — bound to the body, they belong to the inner sphere; yet they are also included within the outer sphere, hence there is an inner and outer distinction. This is called investigating their substance. One further rightly investigates: there are two kinds of in-breath and two kinds of out-breath. When the air enters within, this is called the in-breath; when the air exits without, this is called the out-breath.

items.zh: 復正了知：如是為長入息、出息，如是為短入息、出息，如是息遍一切身分。是名尋思諸息自相。

items.title: Section: Breath-Counting's Remaining Components — All Five Purifying-Conduct Objects Now Complete

items.zh: 又正尋思：入息滅已有出息生，出息滅已有入息生，入出息轉繫屬命根及有識身；此入出息及所依止皆是無常。是名尋思諸息共相。
items.en: One further rightly investigates: when the in-breath ceases, the out-breath arises; when the out-breath ceases, the in-breath arises. The turning of the in-breath and out-breath is bound to the life-faculty and to the body possessing consciousness; this in-breath and out-breath, and what they depend upon, are all impermanent. This is called investigating the universal characteristic of the breaths.

items.zh: 又正尋思：若於如是入息、出息不住正念，為惡尋思擾亂其心，便為顛倒，黑品所攝，是有諍法，廣說如前。與上相違，便無顛倒，白品所攝，是無諍法，廣說如前。如是名為尋思其品。又正尋思：去來今世，入出息轉繫屬身心，身心繫屬入息、出息。如是名為尋思其時。

又正尋思：此中都無持入息者、持出息者，入息、出息繫屬於彼；唯於從因從緣所生諸行，發起假想，施設言論，說有能持入出息者。如是名依觀待道理尋思其理。又正尋思：若於如是入出息念善修、善習、善多修習，能斷尋思。又正尋思：如是道理，有至教量，有內證智，有比度法，有成立法性、難思法性、安住法性，不應思議、不應分別，唯應信解。如是名依作用道理、證成道理、法爾道理尋思其理。是名勤修阿那波那念者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那。
items.en: One further rightly investigates: herein there is no one who controls the in-breath, no one who controls the out-breath — the in-breath and out-breath are simply bound to that body. It is only with respect to conditioned formations, arisen from causes and conditions, that one gives rise to a provisional conception and sets up an expression, speaking of "one who controls the in-breath and out-breath." This is called investigating the principle of the breaths by way of the principle of mutual dependence … This is called the insight, with objects differentiated by the six things, of one who diligently cultivates mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath.

blocks.text: The six-fold investigation applied to the elements and the breath. With this, all five purifying objects have been examined.

subs.head: Substance and marks of the elements

blocks.text: The six elements, inner and outer. "Earth has the mark of solidity… wind the mark of light motion"; "space has the mark of empty space, pervading form, unobstructed". All are "impermanent, and so on through being without self".

"If one fails to understand the differentiated nature of the elements within what appears as a single unified mass, and gives rise to arrogance on account of the body formed by their combination, this is distortion."

"In past, present, and future lives alike, the six elements serve as conditions for entry into the womb." And: "just as grass, wood, and other conditions combine to enclose empty space" and it is called a house, so the elements combine and are called a body.
One knows the in-breath and out-breath as object, "binding the mind" to it. They are found in the body, "bound to the body", yet also belong to the outer sphere.
"When the in-breath ceases, the out-breath arises." The breath "is bound to the life faculty and to the body possessing consciousness"; impermanent.

"Herein there is no one who controls the in-breath, no one who controls the out-breath; they are simply bound to that body." Only with respect to conditioned formations is a "breather" provisionally named.

quiz.q: Investigating "the inner and outer distinction among the six elements" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi divide them?
options: one's own six elements are inner, others' are outer
quiz.why: "One further rightly investigates the inner and outer distinction among earth and the other six elements — this is called investigating the substance of the elements." Master Cháng Bǎi: a being's own six elements are inner; those of other beings are outer.

quiz.q: The space element has "the mark of pervading form." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: space is also a visible colour — e.g., when the sun comes out, all is bright
quiz.why: "The space element has the mark of empty space, pervading form, and being unobstructed." Venerable Miào Jìng: space appears as a visible colour too — when the sun comes out, everything is bright; that is "pervading form."

quiz.q: Not seeing the elements within the unified mass breeds arrogance. What saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: no self within, so I have no ability; no person without, so others have no fault
quiz.why: "If one fails to understand the differentiated nature of the elements within what appears as a single unified mass, and gives rise to arrogance, this is a distortion." Master Cháng Bǎi cites the ancients: "No self within, so I have no ability; no person without, so others have no fault."

quiz.q: "The six elements serve as conditions for entry into the womb." How do the masters map the elements?
options: Miào Jìng: the intermediate being composed of six elements; Cháng Bǎi: the mother's unobstructed birth passage is the space-element condition
quiz.why: "In past, present, and future lives alike, the six elements serve as conditions for entry into the womb." Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the intermediate being, composed of the six elements as condition. Master Cháng Bǎi: first, the mother must have no obstruction of the birth passage — that is the space element as condition. Their mappings differ.

quiz.q: "Two kinds of in-breath and two of out-breath" — which two, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: in-breath and intermediate in-breath; out-breath and intermediate out-breath
quiz.why: "There are two kinds of in-breath and two kinds of out-breath." Master Cháng Bǎi: the in-breath and the intermediate in-breath; the out-breath and the intermediate out-breath.

quiz.q: The breath is "bound to the life-faculty and the conscious body." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the life-faculty?
options: the non-separation of physical and mental organisation
quiz.why: "The turning of the in-breath and out-breath is bound to the life-faculty and to the body possessing consciousness." Venerable Miào Jìng: the non-separation of your physical and mental organisation is the life-faculty; the breath is bound to it.

quiz.q: "No one controls the breath"; it is bound to that. How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate breath and body-mind?
options: the breath depends on the body, and body-mind depends on the breath — mutually bound
quiz.why: "Herein there is no one who controls the in-breath, no one who controls the out-breath — the in-breath and out-breath are simply bound to that body." Venerable Miào Jìng: the breath is bound to the body, and to what is the body bound? Body and mind are bound to the breath — mutually bound.
